title: Run the Accounts Task
subtitle: Create the identity once - idempotently
scenario: It is SD-2. The plan says create the new hire's core accounts by today. Before creating anything, you check the identity store: no account exists for H-4021 yet. Create it once and record the result - the rule that makes a re-run safe.
input: Task: accounts for hire H-4021 (owner IT Provisioner, due SD-2). Identity store lookup for H-4021: no existing account found. Rule: check first, create only if none exists, and record the account id and final state. A re-run must NOT create a second account.
instructions: Record the taskId and whether an existing account was found (existingFound).
Because none was found, set action to created and record the new accountId.
Set the final state to done.
Return one valid JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build one JSON accounts result: taskId, existingFound (boolean), action, accountId, and state. Since no existing account was found, action is created and state is done. Keep existingFound a real boolean.
successMessage: Accounts created. Because you checked first, a re-run would reuse this account instead of making a second one.
editorHelper: Check-then-create: record what you found before what you did.

sections.title: Idempotency is the safety rule
sections.body: Automated provisioning gets re-run - after a timeout, a partial failure, a retry. The rule that makes that safe is check-then-create: look for an existing account before making a new one.

sections.title: Record what you found
sections.body: existingFound is not decoration - it is the evidence the check happened. If it is false you create; if it were true you would reuse. Storing it makes the run auditable.

sections.title: One hire, one account
sections.body: The whole point is convergence: no matter how many times the task runs, the hire ends with exactly one account. Two accounts break offboarding and audit later.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A small accounts result - found, action, account id, state - that the task tracker reads. The medium tier re-runs this after a partial failure to prove the rule holds.
